note: Bright streamer blowout CME to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The CME is visibly wider in STEREO A COR2 imagery than in SOHO imagery. The source of this CME appears to be a complex series of eruptions beginning with an eruption near N05E05 starting around 2025-03-19T00:39Z. This eruption may have triggered additional instability of nearby magnetic field line foot points, which may be associated with the streamer itself. Dimming is clearly seen to the east of the initial eruption location starting around 2025-03-19T06:00Z. It is also around this time that the CME appears to begin to speed up in the SOHO field of view with a more clear/defined front appearing around this time as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on the best fit using SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: Faint and wide loop CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. Source is a filament eruption on or just beyond the NW limb in STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery, likely placing it at a longitude between W120 to W130, and spanning from approximately N10 to N40, with liftoff of filamentary material seen starting at 2025-03-19T03:45Z. Simultaneous opening field line movement can also be seen in STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery, centered at N50, just to the north of the filament eruption, and possibly located further beyond the limb than the filament due to the faintness of this signature. A second, smaller loop of material centered at about N40 can be seen lifting off at 2025-03-19T06:15Z in STEREO A EUVI 304 which may be the source of the additional outflow seen in coronagraph imagery following this CME. Field line movement can also be seen on or beyond the NW limb in STEREO A EUVI 195. The quality and cadence of STEREO A COR2 imagery was affected during time of analysis due to a campaign scheduled to last from 2025-03-18 to 2025-03-24.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using best fit between SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery, as well as the approximated location of the source seen in STEREO A EUV imagery. The quality and cadence of STEREO A COR2 imagery was affected during time of analysis due to a campaign scheduled to last from 2025-03-18 to 2025-03-24.

note: Faint but fast CME with an asymmetrical front, with a protruding nose to the south, seen directed to the west in SOHO with the start covered by the nighttime data gap in SOHO. Its source is the filament eruption seen on/behind the SW limb: as ejecta/prominence in AIA 304 (there are actually two ejectas - a more southern complex shaped loop-like prominence seen at 2025-03-19T22:50Z at latitude of -21, and a fan-shaped ejecta to the north of it seen at latitude of -7 at 2025-03-19T223:46Z. This eruption is also seen as fast opening of field lines behind the limb in AIA 193/171 starting at 2025-03-19T222:01Z and later (starting at 2025-03-19T223:21Z) as bright post-eruptive arcades on/behind the limb in AIA 131. There is an associated long duration occulted C6.0 flare peaking at 2025-03-20T00:07Z from behind the limb (bright arcades). It is possible that the flare is from former Active Region 4018 (S21W100).

cmeAnalyses.note: Updated measurement using the approximated source longitude of former Active Region 14018, which was estimated to be centered near west 100 degrees at the time of this event. The measured parameters may vary slightly due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery.

Since the source is on or behind the limb and STEREO A coronagraph imagery is not yet available because of the nighttime data gap, only a plane-of-sky analysis is possible at this time (although the CME is likely close to the limb and this plane-of-sky measurement may be close to the 3D one).

note: Faint loop CME visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, with a faint flux rope feature more visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is the ejection of material from just beyond the southwest limb, first distinctly seen as a distinct instance of opening field lines and ejecta starting around 2025-03-19T23:15Z in GOES SUVI 304 and 284 imagery. Post-eruptive brightening extends onto the disk spanning from about S10 to S15 and W80 to W90, as seen in SDO AIA 304 at 2025-03-19T23:40Z. Associated surrounding field line movement extends into the northern hemisphere on or beyond the western limb, and some northern deflection occurs as the material erupts.

note: Loop CME with brighter, narrower bulk and fainter shock visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 during a STEREO A COR2 data gap. Faint flickering field lines far off the western limb seen in GOES SUVI 284 suggest that a component of this large scale eruption may be far-sided.

The source for this CME is not observed as a distinct source, but appears to be continued outflow from CME 2025-03-20T17:12Z from AR 14022 centered at N08W75, corroborated via triangulation in the STEREO_CAT tool.

cmeAnalyses.note: StereoCAT measurement using SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO COR2A due to unusable data quality of COR2A running difference imagery in the swpc_cat tool, due to an ongoing STEREO A campaign.

note: Faint CME seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and to the S in two available frames of STEREO COR2A before a data gap begins at 2025-03-21T15:09Z. cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2/C3 only plane-of-sky measurement as available STEREO COR2A running difference imagery quality cannot discern the CME due to an ongoing campaign.

note: Faint halo CME with a bulk visible mainly to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 imagery (more easily seen in difference imagery). There is no STEREO A COR2 imagery for this event due to a data gap. The source of this CME appears to be a large dimming region centered near N02E07 starting around 2025-03-21T15:49Z with a southeast directionality based on the minor EUV wave visible in SDO/AIA 211 and 193 imagery. There's a large coronal hole situated E/SE of the dimming region and a separate coronal hole due west of the dimming region which may have contributed to the deflection visible on the solar disk in SDO/AIA imagery. This source location appears to be a sympathetic eruption to the M1.2 flare from AR14028 (S17W33) seen to the SW in SDO/AIA 131 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on the SHOCK of the CME using SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 imagery. High uncertainty due to lack of stereoscopic viewpoints.

There is clear dimming and moving/opening field lines visible to the SW of the eruption suggesting deflection. This may be due to a coronal hole due north of the source location.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source location.

note: This CME is visible to the north/northwest in STEREO A COR2 imagery starting around 2025-03-28T07:23Z. This event is not observed in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery due to a data gap caused by data processing issues. The source is likely far-sided and may be related to faint field line movement visible beyond the northwest limb in SDO AIA 171 imagery starting around 2025-03-28T06:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of 121 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.

note: This CME is visible to the west/northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided and may be related to field line movement visible beyond the northwest limb in SDO AIA 171 imagery starting around 2025-03-28T12:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This event is visible to the east/northeast in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. This CME is still developing and only early imagery is available as a result. The source is related to an eruption and X1.1 flare from Active Region 14046 starting around 2025-03-28T15:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery. A subsequent wide opening of field lines can be observed in SDO AIA 171 and 193 imagery at this time as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: SHOCK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. This measurement contains a high degree of uncertainty due to the lack of available frames as a result of data gaps in both SOHO and STEREO A COR2.

Measurement of the bulk using several more frames of SOHO LASCO C3 imagery than previously available. There is still only one STEREO A COR2 frame available for this CME, but the fit found using C3 frames the source location aligns well with this one STEREO A COR2 frame.

Measurement of the brighter BULK portion using only 4 early frames. Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. This measurement contains a high degree of uncertainty due to the lack of available frames as a result of data gaps in both SOHO and STEREO A COR2.

note: This CME is visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source appears to be opening field lines beyond the NW limb beginning around 2025-03-29T13:07Z in SDO/AIA 211 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters are based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: Faint loop CME seen to the N in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the NW in STEREO A COR2. The source is opening field lines beyond N limb in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 284, starting at about 2024-03-29T13:10Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source seen in UV imagery and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STREO A COR2.

note: Jet-like CME first seen in the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-03-29T23:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. This CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap from 29/16:53Z to 30/03:38Z. The source of this event is an M1.9 flare from Active Region 4048 (S15E85) seen in SDO AIA 94 and 131. Field line opening is also visible in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3.

note: A very faint loop-like CME to the southeast. There is a series of consecutive faint fronts, one of which is a bit brighter than the others and has been analyzed as the main front, but this brighter front is preceded by more faint fronts. The source of this CME is possibly the M1.5 flare from AR 14048 (S15E80) peaking at 2025-03-30T01:48Z. This CME is preceded by a narrow jet seen at 2025-03-29T23:12Z. It is possible that the jet is associated with the M1.9 flare, while this CME is associated with the M1.5 flare, both from AR 14048. The exact association with flares is not certain. Coronal signatures associated with the flares are relatively minor but very clear: an opening of field lines on/close to the SE limb seen in SDO AIA 193/171 and GOES SUVI 284 around 2025-03-29T23:13Z, followed by post-eruptive arcades seen on the limb in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 284. There is also minor ejecta seen in GOES SUVI 284 around 2025-03-29T23:07Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: A very tentative analysis based mostly on the SOHO LASCO imagery and on the location of the source (but to some degree confirmed by a couple timestamps in STEREO A COR2 imagery in which the front could possibly be seen very faintly after the data gap. The longitude of -85 degrees fits better than -80 degrees.

note: Jet-like CME first seen in the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-03-30T02:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. This CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 in later frames 29/16:53Z to 30/03:23Z. The source of this CME is field line opening seen along or just beyond the NW limb in SDO AIA 171.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2. POS measurement due to source location near the limb and no STEREO A COR2 imagery to triangulate.

note: Faint CME first seen in the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-03-30T02:36Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. This CME is only available in one frame of STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap from 29/16:53Z to 30/03:23Z. The source of this event is a slow prominence eruption seen along the NE limb in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304, along with field line opening seen in SDO AIA 171 and 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Faint CME seen to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2; it is partially obscured by the pylon in C3, but its western edge is seen in SOHO LASCO C3. The source of it is likely an eruption with a very minor ejecta seen in SDO AIA 304/131/193 and GOES SUVI 284 at 2025-03-30T04:07Z just southwest of AR 4048 (S20E70) as post-eruptive arcades and small area dimming. The associated flare is a C3.5 flare observed in GOES-S, not in GOES-P, due to an eclipse.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs. It looks like there is significant southern deflection, since the associated flare is from south of Active Region 4048 that is at latitude of 16 degrees south.

note: Faint CME (somewhat brighter in STEREO COR2 coronagraph than in SOHO LASCO), seen to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. Its source is a filament/ejecta on/close to the northwest limb, seen erupting starting at 2025-03-30T07:48Z in SDO AIA 171/403/131 and GOES SUVI 284/304, and seen as an opening of field lines and later as post-eruptive arcades/brightening in SDO AIA 193 extending to ~N22W70 but possibly centered around the northwest limb or even beyond the limb. The eruption is well seen in STEREO A EUV imagery happening to the east of AR 4035 (N16W94) and centered around ~N22W90.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs and confirmed by the location of the associated filament eruption (close to the NW limb).

note: This CME is visible to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. It is not observed in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap lasting from 2025-03-30T19:09Z to 2025-03-31T03:23Z. The source is likely related to an eruption and M1.5 flare from Active Region 14048 (S15E65) starting around 2025-03-30T23:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery. A subsequent opening of field lines is visible near the southeast limb around this time in SDO AIA 171 and 193 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measured longitude based on the source location. The leading edge of this event becomes too diffuse to measure in later imagery, so this measurement relies on early frames.

note: This event is faint but can be observed to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. It is not observed in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided and may be related to faint field line movement visible beyond the northeast limb in SDO AIA 171 imagery starting around 2025-03-31T08:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees as the source location is far-sided and therefore unknown.

note: This event is visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. It is not observed in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap starting at 2025-04-01T17:53Z. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk at the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location. Additionally, due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 at the time of this event, a triangulated measurement was not available to confirm the measured parameters.

note: Narrow, jet-like CME seen accelerating to the northeast primarily in SOHO LASCO C2 and also farther to the north in STEREO A COR2; the CME is with low confidence associated with a minor eruption with northern deflection from the northeastern side of Active Region 14046 (N10E10) seen starting around 2025-04-02T08:44Z in GOES SUVI 284 imagery, but triangulation suggests that the eruption originates from the far-side, and indeed, moving field lines are seen off the northeast limb primarily in GOES SUVI 284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Two spacecraft leading edge measurement using triangulation to determine the longitude of the source; the CME becomes very diffuse with time and is extremely difficult to see in STA COR2 past 8 solar radii.

note: Faint loop CME seen to the S in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, SE in STEREO A COR2. Source is an eruption seen starting at 2025-04-03T03:24Z from AR 4045 (S15W05) with Eastern deflection. Brightening and ejecta seen deflected to the east as seen in GOES SUVI 304 starting at 2025-04-03T03:24Z. SDO AIA imagery was in a data gap which lasted from 2025-04-02T15:52Z to 2025-04-03T04:54Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement of faint leading edge using several frames of SOHO LASCO C2, C3 and STEREO A COR2. Strong eastern and southern deflection was visible from the source location seen in UV imagery of the Earth-facing disk, which is reflected in the best fit parameters.

note: Faint loop CME seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 and NE in STEREO A COR2. Source is slight dimming seen at 2025-04-03T06:48Z in SDO AIA 193 from N20W15.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using best fit between several frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and two frames of STEREO A COR2.

note: This CME is visible to the E/SE in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 imagery. There is no STEREO A COR2 imagery available for this event due to a data gap beginning at 2025-04-03T15:23Z. The source is a filament eruption visible along the SE limb in GOES SUVI 304 near S25E70 starting around 2025-03-04T17:32Z. Additionally moving/opening field lines are visible in GOES SUVI 171, 195, and 284, as well as brightening which is best seen in GOES SUVI 195. There is a data gap in SDO/AIA during the eruption for this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO imagery and possible source location longitude.

note: CME seen to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A. The source is a filament eruption from sightly over the east limb ~N15, observed as filament ejecta and field line movement starting around 2025-04-04T02:48Z in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A.

note: Very narrow CME seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, which becomes diffuse halfway through the STEREO A COR2 field of view. The precise source is unclear, but several small instances of field line movement on can be seen just beyond the SW limb occurring between 2025-04-04T05:00Z-07:00Z in STEREO A EUVI 195 from a bright cluster of formerly numbered ARs, including ARs 4047, 4040, and 4042, which together span from about latitude S00 to S20 and longitude W90 to W110.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using best fit between several SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 frames. The leading edge becomes diffuse halfway through the STEREO A COR2 field of view.

note: Faint front seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 only due to a STEREO COR2A data gap beginning  at 2025-04-04T10:38Z, better seen in SOHO LASCO running difference imagery than white light. No source for this CME is observed in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky with SOHO LASCO C2/C3 only due to the data gap in STEREO COR2A and no observed source.

note: Faint CME seen to the SSW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and directly S in STEREO COR2A. The source is likely dimming in the far southern area of the disk, centered around S60W20, observed in SDO AIA 193 around 2025-04-04T15:00Z. This may, unlikely, be related to a C4.4 flare from AR 14502 (S23W29) which peaked at 2025-04-04T14:46Z, it is difficult to discern if this flare erupted in this deflected direction, the dimming at S60W20 is an sympathetic eruption, or if the dimming at S60W20 is entirely separate. Thus it is not currently attributed as a source, and noted for completion of the analysis.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A, tracking well with the far southern latitude dimming around S60W20 observed in SDO AIA 193.

note: CME seen to the N in SOHO LASCO C2 and to the N in STEREO A COR2. Source is a filament eruption from just beyond the NW limb. A prominence from just beyond the limb can be seen beginning to liftoff starting at 2025-04-04T16:08Z in GOES SUVI 304. Opening field lines seen in GOES SUVI 284 and ejecta seen in GOES SUVI 304 both show strong northern deflection of this eruption, with ejecta traveling nearly due north. STEREO A EUVI 195 and 304 show that the prominence was centered at about N30 and spanned from W82-W92 (in SDO coordinates).

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement of leading edge using several frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. Strong northern deflection was visible from the source location seen in UV imagery from SDO AIA, STEREO A EUVI, and GOES SUVI, which is reflected in the best fit parameters.

note: Faint outflow-like CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. Source is narrow ejecta and brightening seen at N20W97 (SDO AIA coordinates) in STEREO A EUVI 304 at 2025-04-04T17:45Z. This small eruption may have possibly disrupted surrounding coronal material, resulting in the faint, wide, and slow leading edge which surrounds the narrow flux rope visible in SOHO LASCO C2. This CME overlaps to the south of the preceding CME:2025-04-04T16:36Z. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-04T17:38Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement of the faint leading edge, based on source location seen in STEREO A EUVI and fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-04T17:38Z. The leading edge becomes diffuse only a handful of frames into the SOHO LASCO C3 field of view.

note: Faint CME visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. No clear source of this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit of features in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is some uncertainty due to lack of clear source in available EUV imagery.

note: A bright symmetrical partial halo seen to the east in both coronagraphs. Its source is a clear, wide opening of field lines behind the east limb seen ~2025-04-05T03:55Z in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 284, later followed by post-eruptive arcades gradually appearing from behind the east limb, as seen in SDO AIA 193/304/131. It overlaps with a slightly later CME that is seen as a more full halo in STEREO A.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very approximate analysis of the main brightest front/loop, obtained by fitting with two coronagraphs. Based on the coronal signatures, the source is behind the east limb, but close enough to the limb for the tops of the post-eruptive arcades to start peaking from behind the limb two hours after the eruption.

note: A partial halo CME to the northeast, significantly overlapping with the 2025-04-05T04:00Z CME, and more clearly seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery, in which its front is seen as a separate northeastern halo-like front, following the more eastern front of the earlier 2025-04-05T04:00Z CME. In SOHO its front is harder to trace because of the overlap of two CMEs. Its source is likely far behind the east limb and might be indicated by the large filament behind the northeast limb moving northward, as seen in AIA SDO 304 and GOES SUVI 304 and 284 imagery after 2025-04-05T05:00Z, although this filament is more likely to be the source of a later, more northern, 2025-04-05T09:48Z CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: A very approximate, speculative analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs. The source is likely far behind the east limb and the front is not clear as the CME is largely overlapping with the earlier CME.

note: Faint northward CME with messy multiple fronts, overlapping with 2025-04-05T04:00Z and 2025-04-05T06:36Z CMEs (this overlap makes analysis difficult). The start of the CME is likely significantly earlier, around 2025-04-05T08:36Z, but its front in the early timestamps is very difficult to discern because of the overlap. The source could be the large filament behind the northeast limb moving northward, as seen in SDO AIA 304 and GOES SUVI 304 after 2025-04-05T05:00Z, but it is unclear whether this filament is the source of this CME - or the 2025-04-05T06:36Z CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based solely on the fit with two coronagraphs, since the source is not completely clear and is likely behind the limb.

note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the north in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided, as an opening of field lines is observed over the northeast limb in SDO AIA 171 imagery starting around 2025-04-06T03:15Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the north/northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the north in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely related to an opening of field lines visible over the northwest limb in SDO AIA 171 imagery starting around 2025-04-06T06:30Z. Around this time there is a minor eruption observed near Active Region 14050 (N28W45) which may be associated with this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: Faint and narrow CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. There is no clear source apart from some subtle and slow field line movement visible on the NE limb in SDO AIA 171 around 2025-04-06T16:15Z. The leading edge becomes diffuse partway through the SOHO LASCO C3 field of view. There was no STEREO A COR2 imagery available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which lasted from 2025-04-06T10:53Z to 2025-04-06T17:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-Sky measurement in swpc_cat taken using multiple frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 running difference imagery. The leading edge becomes diffuse partway through the SOHO LASCO C3 field of view. There was no STEREO A COR2 imagery available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which lasted from 2025-04-06T10:53Z to 2025-04-06T17:23Z.

note: Narrow CME with a faint loop-like leading edge visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is no clear source for this CME. The leading edge becomes diffuse partway through the SOHO LASCO C3 field of view.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using several frames of SOHO LASCO C2, and a few frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The leading edge becomes diffuse partway through the SOHO LASCO C3 field of view.

note: Faint and narrow CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery. There is no clear source for this eruption, however, due to its similarity to earlier eruptive activity, it is possible that the source is associated with the ongoing minor field line movement and minor eruptive activity from beyond the E/NE limb. The leading edge becomes diffuse early in the SOHO LASCO C3 field of view. There was no STEREO A COR2 imagery available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-06T20:53Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-Sky measurement in swpc_cat taken using multiple frames of SOHO LASCO C2 running difference imagery. The leading edge becomes diffuse early in the SOHO LASCO C3 field of view. There was no STEREO A COR2 imagery available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-06T20:53Z.

note: This CME is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures visible on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: CME to the northeast with the source and eruption observed slightly beyond the northeast limb starting around 2025-04-07T12:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery. A subsequent opening of field lines is observed over the northeast limb around this time in SDO AIA 171 and 193 imagery, with post-eruptive arcades visible over the eastern limb starting around 2025-04-07T14:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs. The source is behind the northeast limb.

note: Faint CME to the east in coronagraphs, following and overlapping with 2025-04-07T14:00Z CME. It is more clearly seen in running difference imagery than in the white light imagery. The source could be a very minor eruption/post eruptive arcade seen on/behind the east limb in SDO AIA 131/193 at 2025-04-07T14:12Z

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs. The source marked by post eruptive arcades seems to be just beyond the east limb.

note: Fast loop CME seen to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the east-southeast in STEREO A COR2, quickly leaving the SOHO LASCO C2 field of view and comprised of a faint, asymmetric shock seen to the northeast. The likely source is an eruption seen near the vicinity of Active Region 4057 near N10E55 to E65 (after deflection), characterized by a brightening near the footpoints and a subsequent ejection of magnetic field flux seen occurring to the east starting around 2025-04-08T05:45Z, best in SDO AIA 171 and SDO AIA 304. The eruption is also seen, though not as strongly in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 284. Also associated with a type II radio burst with begin time 05:53Z and velocity 456 km/s.

cmeAnalyses.note: Two spacecraft bulk measurement with high confidence in parameters, good fit relative to observed source location.
Shock measurement in SOHO and STEREO A by encompassing the faint northeast edge in both spacecraft as well as the bright bulk.

note: Narrow CME seen to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the east-southeast in STEREO A COR2, quickly leaving the SOHO LASCO C2 field of view. The likely source is a secondary eruption seen near the vicinity of Active Region 4057 near N10E55 to E65 (after deflection) following CME: 2025-04-08T06:00Z characterized by a brightening near the footpoints and a subsequent ejection of plasma seen occurring to the east starting around 2025-04-08T08:00Z, best in SDO AIA 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement using two spacecraft to triangulate the longitude out to 14 solar radii.

note: A super faint minor CME/outflow to the southwest, with mostly the left boundary seen in the coronagraph. It is only seen in SOHO LASCO C2 and in a few early timestamps of C3 because of its faintness and is not discernible in STEREO A COR2. Surprisingly, a clear source for this minor event can be clearly seen on/behind the southwest limb in SDO AIA 171 starting after 2025-04-08T06:42Z - a field line moving very slowly, over several hours, in southwestern direction.

cmeAnalyses.note: The CME is only seen in SOHO LASCO coronagraph and is not seen in STEREO A coronagraph (likely because of its faintness). The source is on or behind the southwest limb, so it is not clear what the longitude of this event is. Only plane-of-sky measurement is possible.

note: Minor CME seen to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 which appears to be associated with an eruption from the eastern limb seen as open field lines starting around 2025-04-08T14:50Z best in SDO AIA 171, 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Updated parameters based on best fit with more imagery.
Preliminary measurement using few frames in both SOHO and STEREO A that don't overlap as the CME continues to propagate outwards to 6 solar radii.

note: This CME is visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 imagery. It is not visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery due to a data gap beginning around 2025-04-08T18:00Z. The source appears to be beyond the NE limb based on moving/opening field lines visible starting around 2025-04-08T20:12Z in GOES SUVI 284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on a plane-of-sky fit using the swpc_cat measurement technique and best fit of CME features.

note: Faint CME with the fuzzy front to the NNE in both coronagraphs, with the front so faint that it is clearly seen in C3 only in a couple of early timestamps and too faint/fuzzy to discern in later timestamps. | Source is a mid-sized filament eruption centered around N26E38, as seen in SDO AIA 304/193, GOES SUVI 304/284 and (close to the NE limb) in EUVI A 304/195 starting ~2025-04-09T05:06Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the location of the source (filament eruption on disk) and confirmed by the fit in two coronagraphs. The longitude can vary a bit (+-5 degrees).

note: A very faint narrow but fast jet to the northeast in both coronagraphs. Its source could be a narrow filament eruption off the northeast limb seen in SDO AIA 304 and GOES SUVI 304 at ~2025-04-09T06:39Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs and confirmed by the approximate location of the likely source - filament off the northeast limb. The jet is seen only in a few timestamps of SOHO and STEREO because of its faintness, so this analysis is very approximate.

note: Faint and narrow jet CME visible to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-09T18:53Z. There was no clear source for this CME; there are several small instances of field line movement in the Western hemisphere of the disk and on the West limb, but none distinct enough to consider as a candidate source.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement of the faint leading edge using several frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and two frames of SOHO LASCO C3. Unable to be tracked farther than two frames in SOHO LASCO C3, due to the C3 running difference imagery being heavily affected and/or corrupt beginning at timestamp 2025-04-09T22:40Z. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-09T18:53Z.

note: Faint CME seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C2. Leading edge begins to become diffuse about halfway through the SOHO LASCO C2 field of view. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-09T18:53Z. Source is opening field lines on the E limb spanning from N00 to N05 and located between possibly E80 to E90, or slightly further beyond the limb, as seen starting as early as 2025-04-09T22:18Z in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location and using only C2 frames, since this CME has not yet reached the C3 field of view. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-09T18:53Z.

note: Faint and narrow CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2; this CME becomes diffuse before leaving the C2 field of view. Source is uncertain, but may possibly be a very faint instance of field line opening seen around 2025-04-09T22:27Z in SDO AIA 171 on the SW limb at S30 with strong southern deflection. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-09T18:53Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement taken using only C2 frames. Leading edge becomes diffuse before leaving C2 field of view. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-09T18:53Z.

note: Faint CME seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A. The source is some filament ejecta from AR 14048 (S16W71) observed in SDO AIA 304 at 2025-04-10T08:12Z, along with field line movement in SDO AIA 171.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement with SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO COR2A imagery. LASCO C2 is not used due to the faintness of the front, it is better resolved in C3 and COR2A.

note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 at 2025-04-10T15:24Z. Also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is most likely some field line movement visible beyond the NE limb best seen in SDO AIA 193 starting at 2025-04-10T14:49Z and in SDO AIA 171 starting at  2025-04-10T14:36Z. The CME is also seen lifting off from behind the NE limb in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2025-04-10T14:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Narrow (<10 degree half-width), jet-like CME first seen to the WSW in SOHO LASCO C2. Also seen to the WSW is SOHO LASCO C3 but is not seen in STEREO A COR2. The source of this jet-like CME is most likely a small but bright eruption in the vicinity of Active Region 14048 starting around 2025-04-10T16:39Z in SDO AIA 304. This eruption can also be seen as a brightening in the vicinity of Active Region 14048 in SDO AIA 171 and SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to lack of triangulation and ambiguity of source location near the W limb. Measurement made with running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 using SWPC_CAT.

note: Extremely faint and narrow CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2. The leading edge becomes diffuse before leaving the C2 field of view. Source is unclear, but there is continual flickering and field line movement from AR 4055 (N08W43), including a small instance of southward directed field line movement seen starting at 2025-04-11T12:45Z in SDO AIA 171. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-11T11:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement of the faint leading edge using four frames of SOHO LASCO C2. Measurement was made using the candidate source longitude, taking into consideration the heavy southern deflection which was possibly indicated in UV imagery. The leading edge becomes diffuse before leaving the C2 field of view. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-11T11:23Z.

note: Faint and wide loop CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2. Source is field line movement and gradual dimming seen from AR 4058 (N18W50) and AR 4055 (N08W45), as well as field line movement seen on the NW limb, starting at 2025-04-11T16:33Z in SDO AIA 171. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-11T11:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location and best fit using several frames of C2 and a few frames of C3. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-11T11:23Z.

note: Wide loop CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2. Source is an eruption near the NE limb, seen as a rising loop of opening field lines starting at 2025-04-11T20:40Z in SDO AIA 171. There are two connected rising loops seen on the E limb, which lift off together in the same eruption. One spans from approx. N22 to N30 along E70, while the other spans from approx. N35 to N50 along E90. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-11T11:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location and best fit in several frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and C3. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-11T11:23Z.

note: CME seen to the SSW in SOHO LASCO C2. Source is opening field lines seen on the SW limb, at S35W90, with some southern deflection in SDO AIA 171 starting at 2025-04-11T22:12Z. This field line movement then disturbs surrounding field lines along the southern limb, as seen in GOES SUVI 284. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-11T11:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using source location seen in UV imagery and several frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and a few frames of C3. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-11T11:23Z.

note: CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and the north of STEREO A COR2. The potential source is activity from the vicinity of ARs 4055 (approx. N06W52) and 4058 (approx. N15W53) characterized by brightening best seen in SDO AIA 193 starting at 2025-04-11T23:13Z and opening/moving field lines best seen in SDO AIA 171/193. The eruption is not seen in STEREO A EUV imagery due to a data gap.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT as well as source location. The CME appears to speed up in later frames. The CME may deflect to the east of the potential source location.

note: CME first visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-04-12T03:24Z. Also visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is likely far-sided as there are not any good source candidates on the Earth-facing disk. A far-sided source is supported by triangulation from SWPC_CAT measurement.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit based on running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-04-12T06:36Z. Also seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is likely far-sided as there are not any good source candidates on the Earth-facing disk. A far-sided source is supported by triangulation from SWPC_CAT measurement.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit based on running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Narrow CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source may be an eruption on or near the east limb in SDO AIA 171/193 as moving field lines around 2025-04-12T07:24Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

note: CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2. Also seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3 (very faint in white light imagery) and STEREO A COR2. This CME is overtaken by the faster CME: 2025-04-12T10:48Z. The source of this CME is likely far-sided as there are not any good source candidates on the Earth-facing disk. There is some very faint field line movement from beyond the WSW limb best visible in GOES SUVI 284 that could be related. A far-sided source is supported by triangulation from SWPC_CAT measurement.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit based on running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-04-12T10:48Z. Also seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is likely far-sided as there are not any good source candidates on the Earth-facing disk. There is some faint field line movement from beyond the WSW limb starting around 2025-04-12T10:24Z best seen in GOES SUVI 284 that could be related to the source of this CME. A far-sided source is supported by triangulation from SWPC_CAT measurement.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit based on running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: CME first seen to the N in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-04-12T12:00Z. Also seen to the N in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is likely a filament eruption beginning around 2025-04-12T11:21Z that is best seen in SDO AIA 304. The filament is centered around N25-35W0-10. Measurement of the CME indicates some deflection toward the NE.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement based on running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 and on visible on-disk source location.

note: CME visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source can be seen on the southwest limb in STEREO A EUV 195 at 2025-04-12T16:00Z with rapid opening of field lines, brightening, and post-eruptive arcades. The eruption can also be seen beyond the limb as an ejecta of material in GOES SUVI 304 imagery. A faster, fainter shock appears to travel ahead of the leading edge of the CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT as well as the source location.
Shock measurement of the fainter feature traveling ahead of the bulk of the CME in the field of view in the coronagraphs.

note: Halo (especially in SOHO) CME, with the start obscured by the nighttime data gap in STEREO A but available from the start in SOHO LASCO. The CME is partly obscured in C3 imagery by the pylon. The CME is directed to the SE in COR2A (as seen after the gap). The source of this CME is a filament eruption extending from N10E15 to S30E15, as seen in SDO AIA 304, 193, 171 and GOES SUVI 284, 304. Post-eruptive arcades are also seen in STEREO A EUV imagery after the end of data gap.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs, fits the area of highest/brightest post-eruptive arcades/dimming (S19E15), but with some southern deflection, it seems.

note: Faint and wide loop CME seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and as an extremely faint halo in STEREO A COR2. Source is a portion of filamentary material seen twisting as it lifts off at S20W30, which is the western-most side of the large filament eruption seen occurring around 2024-04-13T07:00Z. Liftoff of filamentary material is seen in SDO AIA 304 at 2024-04-13T07:10Z and dimming is seen in SDO AIA 193 at 2024-04-13T07:46Z, both from S20W30.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement of leading edge using the candidate source location and the best fit between several frames of SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2.

note: A southeastern halo with a very complex system of several fronts that seem to be moving/expanding in unison. It is difficult to differentiate the bulk vs. shock components of the CME. There seems to be the more dense more southern part to the SW and also a fainter more 'halo' front. The source is a filament erupting starting 2025-04-13T05:00ZZ, stretching from S30E01 to S15W25 as seen in SDO AIA 304 (with more minor dimming reaching S01W30 as seen in SDO AIA 193), and centered ~S18W15.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement of the southernmost lobes of the eruption. Measurement of leading edge using the candidate source location and the best fit between several frames of SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2.

A very approximate, and rather speculative, analysis that encompasses two lobes of this CME seen in STEREO A coronagraph - the more southern earlier lobe and a more northern, closely following, lobe. This analysis is speculative because no corresponding front for the northern lobe was found in SOHO and we are treating the two fronts (or lobes) seen in STEREO A as part of the same event.

note: Faint loop CME seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. This CME overlaps heavily with the large filament eruption CME:2025-04-13T08:00Z. Source is a bit uncertain, but a candidate source is dimming seen near AR 4060 (N09E30) spanning from N00 to N15 and E20 to E30, starting around 2025-04-13T07:00Z in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement of leading edge using the candidate source location and the best fit between several frames of SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2.

note: Narrow loop CME seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. Source is opening field lines seen on the NE limb starting at 2025-04-13T17:00Z in SDO AIA 171 at N20E90.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using a triangulated fit between several frames of SOHO LASCO C2, two frames of SOHO LASCO C3, and a few frames of STEREO A COR2.

note: This CME is visible to the east/southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided and may be related to faint field line movement visible over the eastern limb in SDO AIA 171 and 193 imagery starting around 2025-04-14T13:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: A bright, relatively narrow high southern latitude CME along a streamer to SSW in both coronagraphs.  The CME source is the wide opening/movement of field lines on/behind southwest limb starting ~2025-04-14T14:24Z, as seen in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 284/304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs and confirmed by the coronal signatures (opening of field lines behind the southwest limb).

note: This CME is visible to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely related to an eruption on the southeast limb starting around 2025-04-14T14:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193 and 304 imagery. A subsequent opening of field lines can be observed over the southeast limb around this time in SDO AIA 171 and 193 imagery as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: CME first visible to the S in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-04-14T18:12Z in white light. CME is visible starting a few frames earlier at 2025-04-14T17:36Z in running difference imagery. This CME is also seen to the S in SOHO LASCO C3 but is partially obscured by the pylon. The source of this CME is possibly far-sided. There is not a good source candidate on the Earth-facing disk, but there is some very faint field line movement from on or beyond the S limb best seen in SDO AIA 171 beginning around 2025-04-14T15:42Z. The faint field line movement can also be seen in GOES SUVI 284. Another less likely source candidate is some minor movement starting around 2025-04-14T16:39Z best seen in SDO AIA 193 about S20E10.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement based on running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2. CME is partially visible in C3 but is too obscured by the the pylon to get a good measurement. Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to lack of definitive source candidate.

note: CME first visible to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-04-14T19:00Z. This CME is very diffuse in white light imagery and is easier to see in running difference imagery. The source of this CME is most likely an eruption near the E limb best seen in SDO AIA 304 starting at 2025-04-14T18:19Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement based on running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3.

note: This CME is visible to the south in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery and to the southwest in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures visible on the Earth-facing disk at the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This event is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and is not observed in STEREO A COR2 imagery due to a data gap. The source is likely related to an eruption from S35W85 starting around 2025-04-14T22:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measured longitude based on the source location. Due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery, a triangulated measurement was not available. The measured parameters may vary slightly as a result.

note: This event is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided and may be related to a faint opening of field lines observed over the western limb in SDO AIA 171 and 193 imagery starting around 2025-04-15T03:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely associated with an eruption and opening of field lines visible near or slightly beyond the eastern limb in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery starting around 2025-04-15T14:30Z. Additionally, post-eruptive arcades begin to form around 2025-04-15T17:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 171 and 193 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: Faint CME first seen in the East by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-04-15T23:36Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. This event is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2025-04-15T18:53Z. There is no clear source seen on the disk for this event, aside from some general field line movement seen along the East limb in SDO AIA 171 and 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: POS due to uncertain source location and lack of STA to triangulate

note: Faint CME first seen in the East by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-04-16T00:48Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. There is no clear source seen on the disk for this event apart from some general field line movement seen along the Eastern limb in SDO AIA 171,193, suggesting a likely far sided source.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Diffuse CME with no clear leading edge seen to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and not well by STEREO A COR2; likely associated with a minor eruption occurring near N10W80 in SDO AIA 193, 171 around 2025-04-17T00:30Z as evidenced by moving flux lines, especially in SDO AIA 171.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement with one spacecraft assuming the source location of the source is known; approximately 15 degree longitude uncertainty.

note: Minor CME seen to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2 which appears to be associated with an eruption behind the southeastern limb as evidenced by moving field lines seen in GOES SUVI 284 imagery around 2025-04-17T03:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement using two spacecraft to triangulate a potential far-sided longitude out to 7 solar radii.

note: Narrow jet CME seen to the northeast in just one frame of SOHO LASCO C2 before a data gap obscures the CME; it is seen farther out into the field of view in STEREO A COR2; the CME likely originates from the far-side or just beyond the northeast limb as suggested by triangulation using STEREO A and SOHO imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary leading edge measurement using an isolated SOHO LASCO frame as well as STEREO A COR2 to triangulate the CME; the CME is likely faster than this measurement, but the longitude was largely obtained with this measurement.

note: Jet CME that appears to look like CME: 2025-04-17T09:12Z seen to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2; the CME likely originates from the far-side or just beyond the northeast limb as seen by a fast moving jet of plasma in SDO AIA 304 / GOES SUVI 304 imagery around 2025-04-17T11:37Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement using two spacecraft to triangulate a potential longitude; seen just beyond the northeastern limb in EUV imagery.

note: Very narrow (with <10 deg half-width), faint, fast jet to the northeast in both coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2) mostly seen in running difference imagery (almost not noticeable in white light images). Possible coronal signature (for this likely backsided event) could be minor post-eruptive arcades seen in SDO AIA 304 peaking from behind the NE limb after 2025-04-17T14Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs, setting the half-width to the swpc_cat tool's minimum 10 degrees. The CME is very narrow (narrower than 10 degrees half-width) so the speed could have been underestimated in this analysis.

note: Super faint narrow jet CME to the northwest in SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2, best seen in C3 running difference imagery. No source for it has been found in EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs; analysis is approximate because of the faintness of the front

note: CME first visible to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-04-18T19:36Z. Also visible to the SE in STEREO A COR2 but is obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3. A possible source candidate is an eruption on or near the SE limb starting around 2025-04-18T18:48Z in SDO AIA 304. There is also some field line movement over the SE limb best seen in GOES SUVI 284 starting around the same time. Based on a triangulated measurement using SWPC_CAT, there would need to be a considerable amount of deflection for this candidate to be the source.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement based on running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. CME is obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3.

note: CME first seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-04-19T00:00Z. Also seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C3 but is partially obscured by the pylon. The start of the CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap starting from 2025-04-18T22:38Z to 2025-04-19T02:38Z, and following the data gap the leading edge is out of the field of view. This CME is associated with an M4.4 flare peaking at 2025-04-18T23:50Z and ejecta from on/beyond the SE limb (~S29E90). A Type II radio burst was also observed. The flare and associated ejecta are seen across SDO AIA and GOES SUVI wavelengths but are most clearly seen in SDO AIA 304 and SDO AIA 131. A wider, possible shock front is visible in a few early frames of SOHO LASCO C2, but quickly fades away and was determined to not be measurable. The CME experiences continued southward deflection through propagation.

cmeAnalyses.note: Updated measurement using additional SOHO LASCO C3 imagery. Measurement based on the source location.
BULK measurement based on early frames from SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The CME appears to experience additional southern deflection through its propagation.

note: CME faintly visible to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The CME is partially obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3. The source is likely farsided, and opening field lines can be best seen beyond the SE limb starting at 2025-04-19T06:14Z in SDO AIA 193 and in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA. The eruption is not clearly visible in STEREO A EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

note: Faint and very narrow CME to the east in SOHO LASCO C2, a few frames of SOHO LASCO C3 before it's too faint to track, and three frames of STEREO A COR2 imagery before a data gap. There is no clear identifiable source for this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Half-width may be less than 10 degrees. Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: Semi-faint CME to the south in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 (also visible in GOES-19/CCOR-1). The source is field line movement seen to the south beyond the limb in SDO/AIA 171 and 193 as well as in GOES SUVI 335 starting around 2025-04-19T16:48Z. This is likely a far-sided event. There is no STEREO A imagery for this event due to a data gap.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C3 imagery in SWPC_CAT. No stereoscopic viewpoints of this event.

note: CME first visible in running difference imagery to the S about half way into the FOV of SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-04-19T19:36Z. Also seen to the S in SOHO LASCO C3. CME is covered by a data gap in STEREO A COR2. The CME could be continued outflow following CME: 2025-04-19T17:00Z. A possible source is some faint field line movement to the S starting around 2025-04-19T18:30Z best seen in SDO AIA 171 and SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement based on running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3.

note: CME first seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-04-20T09:24Z. Also seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. This CME overtakes a slower loop originating from close to the same source with a start time of 2025-04-20T08:48Z. The source of this CME is likely a rising loop of plasma seen on/near the SE limb for a few hours prior to the CME start time.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: This CME is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided and may be related to faint field line movement visible over the southeast limb starting around 2025-04-20T18:00Z as seen in GOES SUVI 171 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The leading edge becomes diffuse after a few frames, this measurement relies on early imagery as a result.

note: This CME is visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery but is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap. The source is a filament eruption on/near the northwest limb (centered near N35W80) starting around 2025-04-20T21:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery. A subsequent opening of field lines is visible over the northwest limb in SDO AIA 171 and 193 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measured longitude based on the approximate source location. Due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 at the time of this event, a triangulated measurement was not available. The measured parameters may vary slightly as a result.

note: CME first visible to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-04-21T08:12Z. Also seen to the SE for a few frames in STEREO A COR2 but is likely obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3. This CME is much easier to see in running difference imagery. There is no definitive source for this CME, but there is some general movement from the vicinity of AR 14068 best seen in SDO AIA 193 for a couple hours prior to the CME start time.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

note: CME first seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-04-21T10:12Z. Also visible to the W in SOHO LASCO C3 and for a few frames in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is most likely an eruption near the WNW limb starting around 2025-04-21T08:45Z. It is seen across all SDO AIA wavelengths; however, it is best seen as some brightening and field line movement on the WNW limb in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO COR2A.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit and source location.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using best fit between several frames of SOHO LASCOC2, C3 and STEREO A COR2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

SHOCK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3
