note: Slow, wide CME seen to the west in SOHO LASCO C2 / GOES CCOR1, visible in STEREO A COR2 after a data gap from 2025-05-04T21:38Z to 2025-05-05T01:53Z. Associated with an eruption occurring behind the western limb as seen best in GOES SUVI 284 imagery seen around 2025-05-05T00:08Z with strong opening field lines after 01:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location beyond west limb as well as the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.
Preliminary plane of sky measurement using only a few frames of SOHO LASCO C2.

note: CME faintly seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2 or GOES CCOR-1. The source is not seen in available EUV imagery, and may be farisded.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

note: CME visible to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. The source is a filament eruption centered around S25E20 with liftoff starting at 2025-05-05T08:03Z in SDO AIA 304. Eruption with dimming and opening field lines is best seen in SDO AIA 193. Post-eruptive arcades are best seen in GOES SUVI 284 and SDO AIA 335. The eruption is also visible in STEREO A EUV 195/304 imagery. A faint shock can be seen for a few frames of SOHO LASCO C2 imagery, extending east of the bulk of the CME, but is not measurable.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location as well as the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

note: Narrow CME visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. The source is an eruption near or beyond the east limb as seen in GOES SUVI 304 starting at 2025-05-05T10:40Z as an ejecta of material.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

note: CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. CME partially obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The source is not visible in available EUV imagery and is likely farsided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Updated measurement with more available frames, triangulated between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A.
Preliminary measurement based on one frame of available SOHO LASCO C2 imagery and three frames of STEREO A COR2.

note: Faint narrow CME to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2 and in several early timestamps of C3. The CME is fully covered by the nighttime data gap in STEREO A COR2 and is likely obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. No coronal signatures for this event have been found in EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: The CME is fully covered by the nighttime data gap in STEREO A COR2 and is only seen in SOHO LASCO imagery; no source has been found for this event. Therefore only plane-of-sky measurement (with SOHO LASCO imagery) is possible.

note: A narrowish CME to the northeast in SOHO coronagraph, with a thiner bulk and a possibly slightly wider shock. No clear source has been found for this CME. There is a very minor filament swirling behind/near the NE limb that is seen moving in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 304 after 2025-05-05T21:20Z, however it is not clear whether the filament eventually leaves the sun.

cmeAnalyses.note: The CME is likely fully covered by a nighttime data gap in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph and is only seen in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 imagery. No clear source has been found for this event in EUV imagery. Therefore, only plane-of-sky analysis is possible.

note: CME seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO COR2A, and GOES CCOR-1. The source for this CME may be some weak field line movement observed over the eastern limb in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2025-05-05T22:16Z. The CME front is not first observed leaving the occulting disk, but rather materializing around 2025-05-06T02:48Z in the LASCO C2 FOV best seen in running difference imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement with SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO COR2A frames only, starting at 2025-05-06T07:06Z due to acceleration observed across all measurable frames.

note: A super faint CME with a faint front to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2 (with mostly left boundary visible), the front is hard to impossible to track in STEREO A COR2. No source has been found in EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: The CME front is super faint and is only seen in SOHO LASCO coronagraph. Its source has not been found in coronagraphs. Only plane-of-sky analysis is possible.

note: Relatively fast, narrow eruption seen to the south-southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and farther to the east-southeast or directly southeast in STEREO A COR2; the CME is associated with a filament eruption taking place on the Earth-facing disk near S20W01 seen as a lifting off of dark plasma in GOES SUVI 304 and SDO AIA 304 around 2025-05-06T16:30Z with bright post-eruptive arcades, especially in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement using SOHO/STEREO A out to 12 solar radii reworked to ascertain a maximum latitude.

note: CME seen to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2, C3 and GOES CCOR1. Not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap from 2025-05-06T19:23Z to 2025-05-07T01:53Z. The source is a large-scale filament eruption occurring near N45W20 best seen in GOES SUVI 284 and SDO AIA 304 which begins to lift off as early as 2025-05-06T14:45Z. The full filament liftoff can be seen leaving the disk starting at 2025-05-06T17:00Z. The CME features include a faster protruding nose ahead of the bulk of the CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Updated measurement using additional SOHO LASCO C3 imagery in SWPC_CAT.
Preliminary measurement of the eruption using only SOHO C2 and knowledge of the source location.
Second measurement of the leading edge focusing on the new, brighter feature on the right hound boundary of the CME after 19:00Z.

note: Narrow, faint CME to the northwest in SOHO LASCO and to the north in STEREO A. Its source is possibly an eruption of a small filament north of of Active Region 14079 centered around (N38W30), which is seen as very faint post-eruptive arcades around 2025-06-07T11:15Z in Stereo A EUVI 195 and after 10Z in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs (STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2 and C3). The measurement confirms the source (a minor filament eruption to the north of AR 14079) seen as post eruptive arcades.

note: Bright loop front CME with outflowing material following it to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. The source is a filament eruption in the NE starting around 2025-05-07T11:00Z in SDO/AIA 304, 171, 131, and 193. The filament appears to stretch over the NE limb, possibly by 20 degrees based on a rough STEREO A EUVI 304 calculation. There is limited imagery available in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap for most of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit of brightest front in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. Measured speeds ranged between 200 km/s to 350 km/s.

note: Puff-like CME seen to the north in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and GOES CCOR data; the CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap. The CME probably originates from a far-sided source since there is little evidence of any Earth-directed events on the Earth-facing solar disk.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge plane of sky measurement using only SOHO C2.

note: Outflow-like CME seen to the northeast in SOHO C2 and STEREO A COR2 possibly associated with a partial filament eruption occurring near N37E80 between 2025-05-08T01:30Z and 02:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 193, 171, 304 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement using two spacecraft to triangulate potential latitude/longitude.

note: Jet CME seen to the northwest in SOHO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR1 associated with a point source eruption near the west limb as seen best in GOES SUVI 304 around 2025-05-08T02:05Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement assuming the source is right near the western limb using only one spacecraft (SOHO). The true CME half-width is less than 10 degrees.

note: Loop CME seen only to the east in STEREO A COR2 and not seen at all in SOHO C2 or C3; the source may potentially be associated with an eruption in AR 14079 (N08W44) with strong eastern deflection in which the CME is traveling directly along the Earth-Sun line at the CME is thus not seen in SOHO, or an eruption near the northeast limb seen best in GOES SUVI 284 around 2025-05-08T05:05Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A plane of sky measurement as the CME is not visible in SOHO C2.

note: First of three CMEs seen to the west/northwest in SOHO LASCO C2 and not well seen in STEREO A COR2; the likely source is a minor eruption or series of eruptions in Active Region 14079 (N08W46) with broad moving field lines seen best in SDO AIA 171 between 2025-05-08T07:00Z and 12:00Z and some brightening post-eruptive arcades, especially in the northern extent of Active Region 4079.

cmeAnalyses.note: One spacecraft leading edge measurement assuming that Active Region 4079 is the source of this eruption; the eruption may too be far-sided.

note: Second of three CMEs seen to the west/northwest in SOHO LASCO C2 and possibly seen in STEREO A COR2 as a faint and wide event to the northwest, much faster than the previous CME; the likely source is a minor eruption or series of eruptions in Active Region 14079 (N08W46) with broad moving field lines seen best in SDO AIA 171 between 2025-05-08T07:00Z and 12:00Z and some brightening post-eruptive arcades, especially in the northern extent of Active Region 4079.

cmeAnalyses.note: Two spacecraft measurement using SOHO/STEREO A to triangulate the longitude with medium confidence; probably not far-sided based on fit of the CME seen in one frame in COR2A.

note: Third of three CMEs seen to the west/northwest in SOHO LASCO C2 and not seen in STEREO A COR2A white light but perhaps in one frame in running difference imagery; a possible source is a minor eruption or series of eruptions in Active Region 14079 (N08W46) with broad moving field lines seen best in SDO AIA 171 between 2025-05-08T07:00Z and 12:00Z and some brightening post-eruptive arcades, especially in the northern extent of Active Region 4079.

cmeAnalyses.note: Two spacecraft measurement using SOHO/STEREO A to triangulate the longitude with medium confidence; probably not far-sided based on fit of the CME seen in one frame in COR2A.

note: Faint CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A. The source may be field line movement tracing to around S20W80, observed in SDO AIA 171/193 starting at 2025-05-08T14:40Z. This is the fainter of two concurrent fronts, followed by a brighter CME: 2025-05-08T16:24Z in the same direction which may share this source.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A. Front is quite faint and diffuse, but has good confidence in the high southern latitude.

note: CME which has a fixed point and sprays from due west to northwest as seen in SOHO C2 and not well seen in STEREO A COR2 due to faintness; while the CME may potentially be associated with eruptive activity from AR 14079, the overall source signatures appear minor and thus the CME probably originates from the far-side relative to the Earth-facing solar disk.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge of the left-hand boundary of the CME which appears to be more prominent than its right side as a SOHO plane of sky measurement; the CME is not easily seen in STEREO A imagery.

note: Faint CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO COR2A, and GOES CCOR-1. The source may be field line movement tracing to around S20W80, observed in SDO AIA 171/193 starting at 2025-05-08T14:40Z. This is the brighter of two concurrent fronts, preceeded by a fainter CME: 2025-05-08T15:12Z in the same direction which may share this source.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A.

note: Faint jet-like CME, less than a half-width of 10 degrees, to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and not observed in STEREO COR2A or GOES CCOR-1. The source may be a small filament ejecta on or around the NE limb around N10, observed in SDO AIA 304 starting at 2025-05-09T05:03Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky using SOHO LASCO C2/C3. CME half-width less than 10 degrees.

note: Narrow CME seen to the west in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR1 to the west but not seen well in STEREO A COR2; the source could be associated with a minor eruption from Active Region 14079 (N08W56) but may also be emanating from behind the western limb; there are weakly opening field lines off the western limb seen in GOES SUVI 284 but they do not neatly trace back to an eruption from AR 4079, so analysis is speculative.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge, one spacecraft plane of sky measurement using SOHO C2.

note: Faint jet-like CME, less than a half-width of 10 degrees, to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and not observed in STEREO COR2A or GOES CCOR-1. The source may be a small filament ejecta on or around the NE limb around N10, observed in SDO AIA 304 starting at 2025-05-09T06:12Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky using SOHO LASCO C2/C3. CME half-width barely 10 degrees.

note: Jet-like CME seen to the southwest in SOHO C2, GOES CCOR1, and STEREO A COR2 associated with a very minor filament eruption occurring near S30W65 near 2025-05-09T08:30Z best seen in SDO AIA 304 and GOES SUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Two spacecraft leading edge measurement, which determined the CME was likely far out of the ecliptic. Upper bound on half-width.

note: Faint jet-like CME, less than a half-width of 10 degrees, to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and not observed in STEREO COR2A or GOES CCOR-1. The source may be a small filament ejecta on or around the NE limb around N10, observed in SDO AIA 304 starting at 2025-05-09T10:51Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky using SOHO LASCO C2/C3. CME half-width less than 10 degrees.

note: A faint and narrow CME with unclear brighter bulk front preceded by a narrow possible shock front to the NW in STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1. Its source is not clear. There is some activity from Active Region 14079 in the NW, with some movement of high rising loops, however this movement is going on all morning and there are no clear signs of eruption before the CME is seen in coronagraphs. Alternatively, the source could be behind the northwest limb in STEREO A seen in EUV 195 imagery starting at 14:05Z as faint movement beyond northwest limb.

cmeAnalyses.note: A very approximate analysis based on the fit in two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2). However, the front is so undefined/fuzzy except for 2 images (one in C2 and another in COR2A) that parameters are very uncertain. The source is likely far-sided.

note: Faint jet-like CME, less than a half-width of 10 degrees, to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and not observed in STEREO COR2A or GOES CCOR-1. The source may be a small filament ejecta on or around the NE limb around N10, observed in SDO AIA 304 starting at 2025-05-09T12:51Z or 2025-05-09T14:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky using SOHO LASCO C2/C3. CME half-width less than 10 degrees.

note: A narrow jet, less than a half-width of 10 degrees, fully covered by gap in Stereo A COR2A. No clear source has been found in in EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: The CME is not seen in STEREO A because of the data gap. It is only seen in SOHO LASCO C2 and in a few early timestamps of C3.

note: A fast, high southern latitude, somewhat asymmetrical CME (with a distinct flux rope in evident in running difference coronagraph imagery), seen to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Its source is a significant filament eruption from behind the SW limb, seen in GOES SUVI 304/284 starting  at 2025-05-09T21:01Z off/behind the southwest limb and SDO AIA 171.

cmeAnalyses.note: The CME is only seen in SOHO LASCO imagery and is covered by a data gap in STEREO A imagery. The CME source is behind the southwest limb, so only the plane-of-sky analysis is possible.

note: CME seen to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. A very faint partial-loop (which is the brightest in a series of similar loop-like CMEs (2025-05-09T21:36Z, 23:36, 2025-05-10T01:25, 02:00Z, 03:12, 06:36, 09:48Z). These loops are likely associated eruptive activity AR 4079. Not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2 or GOES-CCOR1. It is possible that 21:48Z loop might be associated with the C1 flare from AR 4079 (N05W64) peaking at 20:21Z or with a very minor filament eruption seen in AIA 304 at 21:09Z (both very minor events).

cmeAnalyses.note: A very uncertain analysis based on the assumption that activity in AR 4079 is the source of this CME and on the front in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 coronagraph. The CME is covered by a data gap in STEREO A.

note: Very narrow (<10 degree width) jet to the northeast seen in SOHO LASCO, practically not seen in STEREO A COR2 because of its faintness. It is preceded by a fainter jet/outflow. One possible source could be a minor bright filament erupting on/behind the northeast limb, as seen in SDO AIA 304 at 2025-05-10T02:00Z, however this seems to be too early for this jet (possibly it is in time for a preceding fainter jet from the same source).

cmeAnalyses.note: Since the CME front is not traceable in STEREO A COR2 because of its faintness and the possible source is a bit uncertain only plane-of-sky measurement is definitive.

note: Very faint high southern latitude CME (or a series of very faint consecutive fronts) that looks like a follow-up for 2025-05-09T21:12Z CME, seen in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3. The front is too faint to be traceable in STEREO A COR2 except for a couple early timestamps. The source of this CME is likely a southern filament eruption close to the SW limb extending from around (S40W75) southward and showing mostly as dimming close to the SW limb see in AIA 193 at 2025-05-10T08:42Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very approximate analysis based on the likely source of this CME (minor filament eruption close to the southwest limb) and confirmed by the two coronagraph fit with the super faint front in STEREO A and with (a more easily traceable) front in SOHO LASCO C2.

note: A high northern latitude CME from near the northeast limb seen in SOHO LASCO and STEREO A, covered by pylon in GOES CCOR-1, and likely associated with the filament eruption/bright ejecta close to the northeast limb (~N40E75) and seemingly directed/deflecting northwardly in EUV imagery, as seen starting in SDO AIA 171/304 and GOES SUVI 304 EUV imagery starting after 2025-05-11T02Z. It is also seen as opening of field lines in GOES SUVI 284 and as minor post-eruptive arcades in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit of the front with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2). There seems to be a northward deflection or rotation going on.

note: A faint CME seen to the north in SOHO LASCO C2 and northeast in STEREO A COR2 in the early time stamps only, with front not clearly seen in C3 at all. The source could be a northern eruption seen as a very faint dimming in SDO AIA 193 at ~N30W05 (east of a small coronal hole) at 2025-05-11T05:40Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2) and somewhat confirmed by the possible coronal signature - faint dimming north of the disk center.

note: A narrow jet seen to the northeast in both coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2, C3 and STEREO A COR2). Its width is likely <10 degrees. A possible source is a minor filament seen erupting on /close to the northeast limb in SDO AIA 304 after 2025-05-11T06:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very approximate analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2). The source is seen on/close to the NE limb.

note: A very faint CME to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2, not seen in C3 because of its faintness. It might be associated with an eruption in the small unnumbered region located at~N20E30, as seen in SDO AIA 193 starting ~2025-05-11T05:21Z as a small area dimming and minor post-eruptive arcades.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit of the faint fuzzy front in two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2) and confirmed by the likely source location (eruption in a minor unnumbered region).

note: Narrow and faint CME seen in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1 to the northeast, with the source possibly a minor opening/movement of field lines behind the northeast limb seen in SDO AIA 171 after 2025-05-11T15:22Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: The CME is only seen in SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1 coronagraphs and not seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is an indication that the source is very far-sided. Only plane-of-sky analysis is possible.

note: Narrow, jet-like CME first seen in the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-05-11T19:00Z, as well as by SOHBO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR in later frames. This event is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap from 11/16:53Z to 12/01:53Z. The source of this event is a small eruption along the NE limb near AR 4087 (N15E80), beginning at approx. 2025-05-11T18:37Z, as seen in GOES SUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: POS measurement due to source near the limb and lack of STEREO A COR2 to triangulate.

note: Narrow CME seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap starting at 2025-05-11T16:53Z. The source is an eruption starting 2025-05-11T20:45Z on or just beyond the E limb, best seen in GOES SUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using SOHO LASCO C2 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

note: Narrow faint CME with a pointy nose to the east in SOHO LASCO, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely a filament eruption off the east limb seen in SDO AIA 304 and GOES SUVI 304 at 2025-05-12T00:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very approximate analysis (+-10 degrees), based on the fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2), taking into account the likely source - a filament off the east limb.

note: A super faint loop CME seen mostly in the running difference imagery to the south-southwest in both coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2). The start of this CME is likely hours earlier. Its front is not seen in C2 and appears in COR2A and C3 after 2025-05-12T04Z, when it is halfway through the field of view.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based solely on the fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2).

note: Extremely faint CME with a fuzzy dimpled front, seen mostly in the running difference imagery to the northeast in both coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2). | No source has been found on disk.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very uncertain analysis based solely on the fit of the left boundary of this fuzzy faint CME in two coronagraphs (STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO).

note: A faint halo seen to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2 and in C3 in the early timestamps, and later seen as almost a full halo in C2, but not seen at all in the STEREO A coronagraph even though imagery is available, and seen very faintly (with no clear front) in GOES CCOR-1. No source has been found for this CME on the Earth-facing disk, indicating its far-sidedness. There is a barely noticeable restructuring of the magnetic field far behind the southeast limb seen in GOES SUVI 284 around 2025-05-12T09Z that seems to confirm the far-sided source.

cmeAnalyses.note: A super approximate analysis based on fitting the halo in SOHO LASCO coronagraph. The CME front is not seen in STEREO A coronagraph at all. The source is likely far-sided.

note: Faint CME seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1, the front fades in the LASCO C2 field of view. The source may be some weak field line movement over the NW limb in SDO AIA 171 starting around 2025-05-12T17:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement due to uncertain source and visibility only in the first 4 frames of SOHO LASCO C2, as it fades into the running difference background afterwards.

note: Bright loop CME first seen in the North by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-05-12T23:48Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is two very large filament eruption, one seen on the Earth facing disk, and the other on the far side. The Earth facing filament has footpoints at approx. N20W50 and N50E60, where as the far sided filament appears to be just beyond the NW limb. These filaments are best seen in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304, along with dimming and field line opening seen in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211 and GOES SUVI 284. In coronagraphs, the on disk eruption appears to over shadow the far sided eruption, and they appear as one feature.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Faint CME first seen in the North by SOHO LASSCO C2 beginning at 2025-05-13T10:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. No clear source is seen on the disk for this event, but initial fits suggest a far sided source.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement base don best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Bright CME first seen in the West by GOES CCOR-1 beginning at 2025-05-13T16:15Z, as well as by STEREO A COR2 in later frames. This  event is currently obscured by a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 which began at 13/14:36Z. The source of this event is an X1.2 flare from AR 14086 (N07W80) seen in SDO AIA 131, along with filament ejecta seen in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304. Wide opening field lines are also visible in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211 and GOES SUVI 284. Associated with a solar energetic particle event at SOHO in the 15.8 MeV-39.8 MeV channel that started 2025-05-13T18:14Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Two spacecraft measurement taking into account the faint and wide feature in STEREO Ahead out ahead of the brighter core portion in addition to the brightest portion of the bulk in SOHO C2/C3 which was required for triangulation to fit relative to the source of the eruption; assumes some eastward deflection due to a coronal hole located just northwest of the eruptive active region.

note: Wide, relatively slow CME seen to the northeast in SOHO C2, C3, and GOES CCOR1 and to the north in STEREO Ahead COR2 clearly associated with a strong far-sided eruption as evidenced by a large-scale prominence eruption occurring off the northeast limb seen best in GOES SUVI 284 seen starting around 2025-05-13T14:05Z but clearly visible more broadly by 15:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Two spacecraft measurement using SOHO and STEREO A with imagery that did not overlap due to an early SOHO data gap and relatively later STEREO A data gap; uncertainty in longitude about 15 degrees.

note: Small outflow-like minor CME seen to the west in SOHO C2 and not in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap; may potentially be associated with a minor eruption from either Active Region 4086 or 4079.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using SOHO C2 as no STEREO A data was present at the time of analysis.

note: Jet CME to the southwest in LASCO C2, associated with a far-sided eruption with opening/moving magnetic field lines seen off the southwest limb in GOES SUVI 284 around 2025-05-13T20:48Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and is visible for one frame in STEREO A COR2 imagery prior to a data gap starting at 2025-05-14T18:53Z. cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source location and the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and one frame of STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. The LASCO C3 pylon obscures CME visiblity in the running difference imagery and it cannot be resolved there.

note: Faint, narrow CME to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is unclear, but may be associated with minor activity from AR 14087 in the NE.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. There may be some uncertainty due to faintness of event.

note: Faint CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2. It is unclear if this CME is also visible in STEREO A COR2 due to data quality as well as GOES CCOR-1 due to obstruction from the control arm. The source appears to be an M2.1 flare from AR 14087 with associated filament ejecta best seen in SDO/AIA 304 and 131.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary measurement based on source location and visible features in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery. Uncertainty with parameters due to limited available frames and faintness of event.

note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-05-15T20:24Z. CME is also visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Also faintly visible for a single frame in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is possibly the more southern portion of some ejecta from a small filament eruption from AR 14087 (N14E40-50) best seen in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2025-05-15T18:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: This measurement is approximate due to lack of available triangulation. The only STEREO A COR2 frame in which this CME is visible is too faint to be usable for measurement. The source location is based on a visible on-disk source.

note: CME first seen in the NNE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-05-15T21:28Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR in later frames. This event only visible in later frames of STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap from 2025-05-25T19:53Z to 2025-05-18T01:53Z. The source of this event is a filament eruption from AR 4087 (N15W42) following an M2.1 class flare which resulted in associated CME: 2025-05-15T18:00Z. This eruption can be seen exhibiting a strong Northwestern deflection in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2

note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-05-16T04:17Z. Also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. The beginning of this CME is covered by short data gaps in both SOHO LACSO C2 and GOES CCOR-1, so the actual start time is likely a few frames earlier. The source of this CME is most likely some field line movement from on or slightly beyond the NE limb best visible in SDO AIA 193 beginning around 2025-05-16T02:00Z. There is also some continuous activity from AR 14087 and AR 14089 that could be related; however, based on measurements, the source is more likely to be the field line movement near the NE limb. This CME partially overlaps with the later CME: 2025-05-16T04:28Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 and on the visible source near the NE limb.

note: CME first visible to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-05-16T04:28Z. CME is also faintly visible in SOHO LASCO C3 and in GOES CORR-1 but is not visible in STEREO A COR2. The beginning of this CME is covered by short data gaps in both SOHO LACSO C2 and GOES CCOR-1, so the actual start time is likely a few frames earlier. CME is much easier to distinguish in running difference imagery. The source of this CME is most likely activity from AR 14090 best seen in SDO AIA 193. Some associated field line movement is visible starting around 2025-05-16T03:30Z. This CME partially overlaps with the earlier CME: 2025-05-16T04:17Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on SOHO LASCO C2 only and on visible source location (AR 14090 S12E75). The frame in SOHO LASCO C3 in which this CME is visible is not clear enough to use in the measurement.

note: Very minor CME/jet first seen in the southeast by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-05-16T08:24Z, and possibly seen in one timestamp of SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery. The source of this event may be a very faint dimming/post-eruptive arcades at around (N25E50) prior to 2025-05-16T08:00Z, best seen in SDO AIA 211.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very speculative analysis based on the fit of a very faint and uncertain front with two coronagraphs in one timestamp. There are very few images with the front of this CME seen in coronagraphs and its source is also very faint and speculative.

note: CME first seen in the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-05-16T10:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is a minor eruption seen along the SE limb in SDO AIA 304 along with field line opening seen in SDO AIA 171, 193 and 211.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. This CME is not measurable in SOHO LASCO C3 as it is blocked by the pylon.

note: Faint CME seen eastward in SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR and STEREO A COR2, but not yet well-formed in C2 until it exits its field of view. Its source is uncertain but is likely one of the many instances of gradual opening of field lines seen on or beyond the SE limb in UV imagery. One such instance of subtle movement can be seen in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 171 around 2025-05-17T21:00Z, located at about S35 on or beyond the E limb.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis using best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Faint narrow CME seen to the east in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. Not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1. No source for it was found in EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: This analysis is based on the fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2).

note: Faint CME to the west in SOHO LASCO, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. No source has been found in EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs (STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO).

note: Faint CME to the west, only seen in a few early timestamps of STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2. Also visible in GOES CCOR-1. This CME seems to follow in the footsteps of 2025-05-18T12:36Z CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2).

note: Narrow high northern latitude jet for which only the right boundary is seen (not the whole loop) to the north in SOHO LASCO C2 and possibly to the north-north-east in STEREO A COR2. Not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1. The full loop is faintly seen in C3 for quite a few timestamps. No source has been found for this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: A very speculative analysis of this very faint event  without a found source. Analysis is based on the fit of the very faint and incomplete front in two coronagraphs, SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2.

note: Large, bright CME first seen in the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-05-19T00:00Z as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a large filament eruption centered at approximately N50E10 with a gradual liftoff beginning at approximately 2025-05-18T19:00Z. This filament can be seen exhibiting some Northwestern deflection in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304, along with dimming visible in SDO AIA 193 and 211, field line opening visible in SDO AIA 171 and post eruptive arcades visible in SDO AIA 131 and 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. This CME appears to speed up in later frames.

note: CME first seen in the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-05-19T09:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This event is too faint to be seen in STEREO A COR2. The source of this event is an M3.2 class flare from along the Eastern limb (N25E90) as seen in SDO AIA 94 and 131. Opening field lines are also visible in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: POS measurement due to lack of STEREO A COR2 imagery and source near the East limb. Event fades before leaving the FOV in SOHO LASCO C2.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of 90 degrees due to the unknown source location.

note: CME first seen in the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-05-19T12:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is brightening and field line movement along the NE limb as seen in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

An opening of field lines can be observed over the eastern limb at this time in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: CME observed to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and additionally to the west for 3 frames of STEREO A COR2 after a data gap from 2025-05-20T12:38Z-16:38Z; data gap resuming at 2025-05-20T17:09Z. cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

Also observed well as field line movement in SDO AIA 171/193. Visible deflection of the ejecta southward is observed in the SDO AIA and GOES SUVI field of view. This is the first of two overlapping CMEs from this same source, preceeding the slower CME 2025-05-20T20:12Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Single spacecraft 3D measurement with SOHO LASCO C2 only. STEREO A COR2 not available due to a data gap, and the LASCO C3 pylon greatly obscures the CME front in white light and running difference imagery. As such, the latitude and longitude may vary +- 10 degrees in either direction, with good confidence in the southern deflection from the observed source via SDO AIA and GOES SUVI imagery.

note: CME observed to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap spanning 2025-05-20T17:09Z to 2025-05-21T01:23Z. The source is an on-disk filament eruption and brightening centered around S35E55 in SDO AIA 304 and GOES SUVI 304 beginning around 2025-05-20T19:39Z. Also observed well as field line movement in SDO AIA 171/193. Visible deflection of the ejecta southward is observed in the SDO AIA and GOES SUVI field of view. This is the second of two overlapping CMEs from this same source, following the faster CME 2025-05-20T20:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Single spacecraft 3D measurement with SOHO LASCO C2 only, becoming notably more faint after several frames. STEREO A COR2 not available due to a data gap, and the LASCO C3 pylon greatly obscures the CME front in white light and running difference imagery. As such, the latitude and longitude may vary +- 10 degrees in either direction, with good confidence in the southern deflection from the observed source via SDO AIA and GOES SUVI imagery.

note: Faint and narrow CME to the east in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and GOES CCOR-1. Not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap from 2025-05-20T17:09Z to 2025-05-21T01:23Z. Source is possibly beyond the eastern limb based on field line movement starting around 2025-05-20T20:00Z as seen in GOES SUVI 284. An additional potential source includes minor movement from AR 14093 (~S06E65) as seen in available SDO/AIA imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters are based on a best fit using a plane-of-sky method in SWPC_CAT.

note: This CME is visible to the east/northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is related to an eruption from Active Region 14093 (~S06E60) starting around 2025-05-21T08:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery. An opening of field lines is visible over the northeast limb at this time in SDO AIA 171, 193, and GOES SUVI 284 imagery as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely related to a filament eruption observed beyond the west limb as seen in GOES SUVI and STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery starting around 2025-05-21T13:15Z. A faint but wide opening of field lines can be observed over the southwest limb in GOES SUVI 284 around this time as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. Because the source is far-sided, a precise source location is unknown and the measured parameters may vary slightly as a result.

note: Very faint front seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2. This is one of several successive faint fronts associated with a gradual streamer blowout seen to the NE. Gradual opening field line movement can be seen in GOES SUVI 284 over the course of several hours during this blowout. The faint leading edge becomes diffuse before reaching edge of the SOHO LASCO C2 field of view. Obstructed by pylon in GOES CCOR-1. Not discernable in STEREO A COR2 due to faintness.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of Sky measurement of faint front using five frames of SOHO LASCO C2 running difference imagery. This faint leading edge becomes diffuse before reaching the edge of the SOHO LASCO C2 field of view. Obstructed by pylon in GOES CCOR-1. Not discernable in STEREO A COR2 white light and running difference, due to faintness.

note: Faint jet-like CME to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, possibly faintly to the N in STEREO A COR2 and NW in GOES CCOR-1. This CME overlaps with a developing streamer blowout CME to the north in the coronagraphs. The source appears to be a faint and quick eruption associated with moving/field lines and brief dimming as seen in SDO/AIA 193 starting around 2025-05-22T08:10Z from the now decayed Active Region 14089 in the NW.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit in relation to source location. Parameters may vary by +/- 10 degrees due to overlapping features in coronagraph imagery.

note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-05-22T15:36Z. CME also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. CME seen to the NNE in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is most likely an eruption on or slightly beyond the NE limb beginning around 2025-05-22T15:00Z. The eruption and moving field lines can be seen across SDO AIA and GOES SUVI wavelengths; but the associated ejecta is best seen in SDO AIA 304, and the moving field lines over the NE limb are best seen in GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement is speculative. Imagery in LASCO C2 is only available in early frames, and LASCO C3 is only available in later frames. Imagery from STEREO A COR2 is very grainy.

note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-05-23T06:24Z. Also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. This CME partially overlaps with continued outflow and rising loops at the back of CME: 2025-05-22T15:36Z. The source of this CME is most likely a filament eruption on or near the NE limb best seen in SDO AIA 304 beginning around 2025-05-23T05:00Z. The prominence can be seen building over the NE limb for several hours prior to its eruption.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement based on triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 and visible source location on/near the NE limb.

note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-05-23T10:00Z. Also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. CME might be visible in GOES CCOR-1 but is difficult to distinguish from earlier filament eruption CME: 2025-05-023T06:24Z. The source of this CME is somewhat ambiguous but is most likely some continued rising loops following CME: 2025-05-22T15:36Z and the filament eruption CME: 2025-05-23T06:24Z. These can be seen for several hours before and after the CME start time.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit based on triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 and visible source location.

note: Bright CME to the west in STEREO A COR2 imagery associated with a faint shock more easily seen as a halo in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is a far-sided filament eruption starting around 2025-05-23T16:45Z as seen in STEREO A EUVI 304 and briefly visible to the S/SW in GOES SUVI 304 starting around 2025-05-23T18:29Z and SDO/AIA 171 around 2025-05-23T17:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the BULK of the CME. Parameters are based on best fit relying more heavily on STEREO A COR2 imagery to differentiate the bulk and shock features.

Measurement of faint SHOCK feature. Parameters based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. A portion of the shock front to the NW from SOHO LASCO C3's field-of-view was excluded from this fit due to measurement technique limitations.

note: CME first seen in the SW by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2025-05-23T17:38Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR in later frames. There is no clear source for this event, as it is likely far sided. This CME heavily overlaps with far sided halo CME: 2025-05-23T16:53Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A plane-of-sky measurement due to far side source location and lack of reliable fit between STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3.

note: Fast jet with a fuzzy front seen to the southwest in SOHO LASCO and to the south in STEREO A COR2 and not seen in GOES CCOR-1. Its source is likely the 2025-05-24T03:31Z eruption in the plage located in the middle of the large southern coronal hole that crossed the central meridian on 2025-05-15. The eruption was seen as brightening, dimming and post-eruptive arcades in SDO AIA 193 and 304 and is loosely centered around S45W32.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the best fit of this narrow jet with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2) and confirmed by the location of the likely source (filament eruption). It looks like the CME is deflecting southward.

note: Very faint slow CME, a partial halo in SOHO LASCO C2, with a messy front consisting of multiple consecutive faint unevenly shaped fronts, seen extremely faintly to the northeast in SOHO LASCO and a bit more clearly to the northwest in STEREO A COR2. Not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1. To satisfy this constraint - NE in LASCO, NW in STEREO - its longitude has to be between -155 and -175 degrees, so likely this is a very far-sided event. No clear source for it was found in EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2) and supported by the range of possible longitudes (based on the CME appearing northeast in LASCO and northwest in STEREO A). This analysis is based on the clearer second front directly following a messier first front of the CME, as they appear in both coronagraphs.

note: Narrow, jet CME first seen in the West by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-05-24T11:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This event is not visible in STEREO A COR2. The source of this event is a C5.9 flare and minor eruption from AR 4098 (S05W32) as seen in SDO AIA 171, 193 and 211.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3

note: Jet-like CME first seen in the West by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-05-24T18:36Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This event is not visible in STEREO A COR2. The source of this event is a C5.3 flare and subsequent eruption from AR 4098 (S05W40) seen exhibiting Western deflection in SDO AIA 193 and 211.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3.

note: Jet like CME first seen in SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-05-24T21:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2. The source of this event is an M2.1 flare and minor eruption from AR 4098 (S05W40) seen in SDO AIA 131, 193 and 211.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3.

note: CME observed to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and faintly in STEREO COR2. The source is the X1.1 class flare from AR 14098 which began at 2025-05-25T01:40Z, also observed as some field line movement in SDO AIA 171/193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Difficult triangulation with SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, as STEREO A COR2 data quality and the diffuse front directed towards STEREO A made for tough visibility in running difference imagery. Triangulated north and west of the observed source region at S06W45, indicating some deflection.

note: Faint CME overlapping a streamer blowout to the east, observed in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is likely a filament eruption and brightening in SDO AIA 304 at 2025-05-25T02:54Z, and a double peaked C5.3 and C6.4 flare observed on/just beyond the east limb starting at 2025-05-25T02:50Z in SDO AIA 131. Also observed as some field line movement in SDO AIA 171/193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. E90 is the triangulated longitude and this is not plane-of-sky. Due to the faint front and overlap with a concurrent streamer blowout, the earliest visible frames are omitted for a better tracking of the front.

note: Narrow jet with a fuzzy front overlapping with/partially obscured by the previous western jet, and seen to the west as a narrow jet both in SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source could be the Active Region 14098 (S05W48 at the time) that has been active all day, but there is also a slow eruption/ejecta to the west of this active region (at longitude of ~80 degrees), as seen in SDO AIA 304 imagery starting around 2025-05-25T13:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit in two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2) and confirming the source as the filament eruption significantly east of Active Region 14098.

note: Narrow faint jet to the west in SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and (most likely) in STEREO A COR2, overlapping with/partly obscured by an earlier jet/outflow seen to the west. There is a possible very faint shock in C2 that is wider than the narrow denser bulk. The source of this CME is likely the M8.9 flare from Active Region 14098 (S05W50) peaking at 2025-05-25T16:30Z and the associated filament eruption seen as ejecta starting at 2025-05-25T16:43Z in SDO AIA/GOES SUVI 304 and SDO AIA 193 and as dimming in EUVI A 195 and SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: A highly speculative measurement based on the location of the flare and the front in SOHO LASCO C2, adjusted for what is possibly the faint front in STEREO A COR2. The front in COR2 is extremely faint and is difficult to ascertain and the analysis is hence speculative.

note: A very narrow faint jet seen to the west in SOHO LASCO C2 and not seen in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph. The source could be activity in AR 14098 but no clear coronal signatures could be pinpointed.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky analysis of this faint narrow jet that is only seen in SOHO LASCO coronagraph and for which no clear source could be found. The width of this CME could be even narrower than 10 degrees.

note: Faint narrow CME/outflow with unclear front overlapping with/obscured by outflows from the previous CME in this direction, faintly seen in SOHO, STEREO A COR2 and in CCOR-1. No source has been found in EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very approximate analysis based exclusively on the best fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2), since no source has been found in EUV imagery.

note: Narrow faint jet with a fuzzy/dimpled front to the E in SOHO LASCO C2, also faintly seen in STEREO A COR2. Not clearly seen in GOES CCOR-1. The front becomes more clear in later frames, especially in SOHO LASCO C3.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very approximate analysis based on the fit in two coronagraphs.

note: A relatively bright CME seen to the east in all three coronagraphs. Its source is the M1.4 flare from AR 14100 (N12E70) and the associated ejecta seen in SDO AIA/GOES SUVI/EUVI A 304 around 2025-05-26T13:21Z (ejecta directed northward). Coronal signatures include intense dimming, brightening, post-eruptive arcades and even a wide EUV wave seen almost reaching the central meridian in SDO AIA.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the location of the flare/eruption (AR 14100) and the best fit with two coronagraphs, SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2.

note: Narrow fast jet to southeast in both coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2). Not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1. Its source could be a very minor ejecta seen on/close to the southeast limb in STEREO A EUVI 304 at 2025-0-26T15:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2).

note: Wide CME observed to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is a broad opening of field lines to the northeast centered on disk around N15E61, north of AR 14100 (N08E61), observed best in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 284 beginning slowly around 2025-05-27T07:16Z and faster starting around 2025-05-27T08:06Z. Accompanied by some slight dimming in SDO AIA 193 well north of this central point, spanning a thin arc ~N35E90 to ~N35E40, then down to ~N08E33. This minor increase in brightening is associated with a brief post-eruptive arcade seen from Active Region 14100 and is accompanied by a long-duration post-eruptive brightening from the surrounding area near and around Active Region 14100. Long-duration post-eruptive brightening near and around Active Region 14100 can be seen in SDO AIA 131. Two brief brighter arcades forming at Active Region 14100 resulted in a C4.5 and a C5.0 flare.

cmeAnalyses.note: SHOCK measurement of the more faint outer feature, triangulated between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.
BULK measurement of brighter inner feature, triangulated between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Faint loop CME visible to the S/SE in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and GOES CCOR-1 and to the SE in STEREO A COR2. Source is field line movement on or near the SE limb seen in GOES SUVI 284 around 2025-05-27T15:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between several frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery.

note: Narrow, fast, spray CME seen to the due west in SOHO C2, C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2A which appears to emanate from higher and higher latitudes with time; the source is an eruption just beyond the western limb as seen by moving field lines in GOES SUVI 284 occurring around 2025-05-28T02:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement encompassing the CME's path traversing the ecliptic plane as the CME pitch angle increases with time.

note: Narrow CME seen to the due west in SOHO C2, C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2A; the source is unclear but may be associated with an eruption beyond the western limb as seen by moving field lines in GOES SUVI 284 occurring around 2025-05-28T07:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement using SOHO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 for triangulation.

note: CME first seen in the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-05-30T00:36Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a small eruption seen located at approx. N15W65 exhibiting a Northern deflection. This eruption can be seen vaguely in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304, but post eruptive arcades are seen in SDO AIA 94, 193, 211 and STEREO A EUVI 195 and 304, more clearly.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: CME with hazy leading edge first seen in the East by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2025-05-30T06:38Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is an M3.4 class flare from AR 4100 (N05E21) as seen in SDO AIA 131. A wide area of dimming is also visible in SDO AIA 193 and 211, along with field line opening seen in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Jet-like CME first seen in the SE by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2025-05-30T06:53Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is minor field line movement seen along the Southeast limb in SDO AIA 171, 183 and 211.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. This event is too faint to be reliably tracked in SOHO LASCO C3.

note: Narrow, jet-like CME first seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-05-30T08:00Z. Also seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. A possible source is an eruption from plage region 14093 (S06W61) beginning around 2025-05-30T07:12Z in SDO AIA 304 that appears to be deflected northward. The same eruption is visible in STEREO A EUVI imagery just to the SW of center disk. This would explain why the CME is not visible in COR2A (it is mostly nose on from the perspective of STEREO A and quite narrow).

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on visible source location.

note: Narrow, jet-like CME first seen to the W in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2025-05-30T10:23Z. CME also seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is most likely an eruption that is visible near the W limb from the perspective of STEREO A. The eruption is seen in STEREO A EUVI 304 and 195 beginning around 2025-05-30T09:35Z near the W limb.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 and on visible source location in STEREO A EUVI.

note: Hazy CME first seen to the SE in STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2025-05-30T12:53Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this CME appears to be continued dimming and field line movement following a wide eruption associated with an M3.4 class flare from AR 4100. These features can be seen clearly in SDO AIA 211. This CME overlaps with earlier CME: 2025-05-30T06:38Z which is associated with the M3.4 flare, where as this event is more associated with the subsequent dimming following the flare.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. This event is not measurable in SOHO LASCO C3 as it is obscured by the pylon.

note: Full-halo CME first seen in GOES-19 CCOR-1. Also seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 after the beginning of a downlink period with data streaming in starting at about 2025-05-31T01:00Z. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-05-30T19:09Z. The source is an M8.1 flare from AR 14100 (N12E12). A significant area of opening field lines and dimming can be seen from near AR 14100 (N12E12) in SDO AIA 193/171/131/304 and GOES SUVI 284/304 beginning at 2025-05-30T23:47Z, immediately after the flare. Dimming and field line movement extends along a nearby filament which spans across most of the Earth-facing disk, stretching from approximately N30E05 to S15W35, snaking through the entire NW quadrant of the Earth-facing disk in a shape resembling the number '3'. It appears that most of the filamentary material ejected is from the upper lobe of the '3', and departs from approximately N10W15.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary analysis of the SHOCK using about four frames of GOES CCOR-1 and four frames of SOHO LASCO C3.
Analysis of the BULK using about four frames of GOES CCOR-1, four frames of SOHO LASCO C3, and two frames of STEREO A COR2.

Preliminary measurement using the only imagery available at the moment, which is four frames of GOES-19 CCOR-1. Measurement made by taking a preliminary best fit with reference to source location observed in UV imagery of the Earth-facing disk.

note: Jet like CME first seen in the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-05-31T03:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR in later frames. The source of this event may be related to a minor eruption from AR 14104 (N06E41), exhibiting Eastern deflection. This eruption can be seen in SDO AIA and STEREO A EUVI 304, along with brightening seen in SDO AIA 94, 131 and field line movement in SDO AIA 171 and 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Jet like CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-05-31T04:48Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR in later frames. The source of this event is eruptive activity and brightening seen from AR 14104 (N06E41) as seen in SDO AIA 94, 171, 193 and 211.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Very faint CME first seen to the South in SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-05-31T07:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1 and to the SE in STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is likely continued dimming and field line movement seen following a large eruption from AR 14100. This dimming can be seen centered at approx. S20E05 in SDO AIA 211. No arrival signature was seen in solar wind at L1, however this CME may have been swept into the combined front by a later faster 2025-05-31T14:23Z CMe.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. This CME is too faint to be reliably measured in SOHO LASCO C3.

note: Jet-like CME first seen in the East by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-05-31T09:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR in later frames. The source of this event is M4.5 flare and minor filament eruption from AR 4100 (N10E05) as seen in SDO AIA 131. STEREO A EUVI imagery suggests strong Eastern deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: CME first seen in the Southeast by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2025-05-31T11:53Z. This event is not clearly seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1. The source of this CME is a small filament eruption seen located at approx. S25E40, beginning at approx. 2025-05-31T10:55Z as seen in SDO AIA and STEREO A EUVI 304. Dimming and field line movement is also visible in SDO AIA 171 and 211.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in STEREO A COR2. This CME was not visible to measure in SOHO LASCO C2/C3.

note: Partial halo CME first seen in the East by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2025-05-31T14:23Z. This CME is seen VERY faintly in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR as a full halo signature in later frames. There is no abundantly clear source for this event. There is a small region of brightening and field line movement from AR 14100 (N15E08) beginning at approx. 2025-05-31T13:34Z as seen in SDO AIA 94 and 211 that may be associated with this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit in STEREO A COR2 and low confidence fit in GOES CCOR. This CME does not reliably appear in SOHO LASCO C2/C3.

note: Faint loop CME first distinguishable as a coherent front to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 at 2025-06-01T18:00Z. There is no clear source in available UV imagery. There are several extremely faint, outflow-like fronts seen to the SW around this time. This front is the most cohesive and is visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using several frames of SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1.

note: Narrow faint loop CME to the southwest in both coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2). Not clearly seen in GOES CCOR-1. Its start could be earlier but no clear front is seen in SOHO LASCO C2. No clear source has been found for this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs, as no clear source has been found.

note: A series of multiple fronts to the northwest seen in both coronagraphs. Its source is an eruption behind the northwest limb seen as opening of field lines behind the limb in SDO AIA 193 starting at 2025-06-02T06:51Z. This eruption is also seen in EUVI STEREO A 195 on disk, close to the northwest limb (N15W68 in STEREO A) as dimming and post-eruptive arcades around 2025-06-02T07:05Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

note: The more western, faint lobe of the CME: 2025-06-13T:25Z. The front of this faint western lobe is very faintly seen only in SOHO LASCO C3 coronagraph (mostly in running difference imagery), while it is covered by the data gap in STEREO A COR2. Not clearly seen in GOES: CCOR-1.

cmeAnalyses.note: The CME/CME lobe is only seen (and faintly) in SOHO LASCO and no clear source has been found for this CME, so only plane-of-sky measurement is possible for it.

note: CME visible to the N in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and slightly to the NE in STEREO COR2. The source is uncertain, but may be a wide area of slowly opening field lines visible in the NW portion of the Earth-facing disk, centered at approximately N50 and extending from W90 to possibly as far as E10 (it is difficult to tell given the faintness of the field line movement on the disk) as seen in GOES SUVI 284 starting as early as 2025-06-02T11:30Z. Analysis of this CME was affected by a data gap in STEREO A COR2 which lasted from 2025-06-02T23:53Z to 2025-06-03T00:53Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using multiple frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and two usable frames of STEREO A COR2. Analysis of this CME was affected by a data gap in STEREO A COR2 which lasted from 2025-06-02T23:53Z to 2025-06-03T00:53Z, resulting in there being two usable frames before the tracked feature exited the STEREO A COR2 field of view.

note: A slow CME to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2, seen more brightly in COR2A and appearing as a faint partial halo in CCOR-1. Its start time could possibly be even earlier, but the clear front is seen closer to 2025-06-03T07:48Z. Its source could be an eruption of a filament in the north/northeast, seen in SDO AIA 193/304 and EUVI A 195/304/284 starting at ~2025-06-03T01:21Z. Initial dimming and faint post-eruptive arcades are centered around ~(N20E01), but later the dimming is seen migrating/expanding eastwardly through the rest of the morning, and settling on a large circular area centered ~N35E15 by 2025-06-03T12:20Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis of the first closed loop front (not the initial dimpled/broken/fuzzy front) based on the best fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2). This analysis is approximate, as longitude of the fit can vary from -17 to 27 degrees.

note: Narrow faint CME/outflow to the northeast in STEREO A COR2 and to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C3. Not clearly visible in GOES:CCOR-1. No source has been found for this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit of this narrow CME in two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2). No source was found for this event, however it is worth noting that the CME latitude and longitude are just north of the recently opened coronal hole which was gradually 'opened' by a very slow motion eruption associated with the 2025-06-03T07:48Z CME.

note: Narrow very faint CME with a fuzzy front seen to the northeast in SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs and obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. Its source is the filament eruption centered ~(N23E45) starting at 2025-06-04T10:17Z as seen in SDO AIA 193/304 as dimming and as opening of field lines on the northeast limb in STEREO A EUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit of the fuzzy faint front in two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2).

note: Faint, diffuse CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. Not clearly seen in GOES CCOR-1. The source may be associated with a quick eruption and field line movement from an area near N12E60 as seen in SDO/AIA 193 starting around 2025-06-04T17:15Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The parameters may vary by +/- 10 degrees due to the faintness of the CME.

note: Bright CME first seen in the Northeast by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-06-05T08:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a far sided filament eruption seen faintly in GOES SUVI 304. Field line movement is also visible along the NE limb in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: CME seen to the south in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and to the southeast in STEREO A COR2. The source is nearly continuous, gradual, and wide field line movement seen on and near the south limb of the Earth-facing disk as seen in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 284. This eruption is preceded by a slower outflow of material which was similar in appearance, though more diffuse, and sourced from at or near the same location near the southern limb of the Earth-facing disk.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using several frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery.

note: Extremely faint jet CME visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The leading edge is extremely diffuse. The source is associated with narrow field line opening seen on the NW limb around N35 which traces to either to a small area of post-eruptive brightening seen at N35W75 in SDO AIA 171 starting at about 2025-06-06T08:21Z or possibly to beyond the NW limb. Very subtle field line movement in the vicinity of N35W75 can also be seen in STEREO A EUVI 195, but there are several subtle instances of field line movement in the area of the disk, therefore it is difficult to identify an exact source.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement was using four frames of STEREO A COR2 imagery, before the leading edge becomes too diffuse to track. After several attempts, the leading edge of this CME is not reliably trackable in SOHO LASCO C3, C2, or in GOES CCOR-1; the leading edge is too diffuse or is not discernable in the imagery. The leading edge is visible and reliably trackable for a few frames in STEREO A COR2.

note: Faint and wide CME to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. Source is an eruption centered near N12E37 starting around 2025-06-06T10:50Z, as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 and GOES SUVI 284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using triangulation between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 and source location seen in UV imagery of the disk. This CME was partially obstructed by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1.

note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is likely related to a large dimming region centered near N10E40 which begins to appear around 2025-06-08T01:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 171 and 193 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the south in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely related to a filament eruption visible beyond the southwest limb in SDO AIA 304 imagery which hovers for a few hours before lifting off around 2025-06-08T05:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely related to an eruption visible near the northeast limb starting around 2025-06-08T12:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is faint but visible to the west/southwest in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery for a few frames before becoming too diffuse to observe. Not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2 or GOES CCOR 1. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of 90 degrees due to the uncertain source location.

note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-06-08T21:36Z. CME is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. CME is seen to the NNE in STEREO A COR2 for two very faint frames. There is some significant deflection toward the N later into the propagation through the FOV of SOHO LASCO C3. The source of this CME is like an eruption from over the NE limb visible in SDO AIA 304 beginning around 2025-06-08T21:22Z. The eruption is also seen as moving field lines from beyond the NE limb in SDO AIA 171. The CME is overlapped at the back by later CME: 2025-06-08T22:12Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and one faint frame in STEREO A COR2 as well as visible source location over the NE limb.

note: CME first seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-06-08T21:48Z. CME also seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. There is likely some deflection early in the propagation into the FOV of SOHO LASCO C2. The source of this CME is likely a loop seen rising from beyond the W limb and some moving field lines best seen in SDO AIA 171 beginning around 2025-06-08T20:27Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 as well as visible source beyond the W limb. The couple of visible frames in COR2A help with triangulation, but the front itself is not defined enough to be used in the measurement.

note: Very narrow (less than 10 degree half-width) jet-like CME visible to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-06-08T21:48Z. 2025-06-08T22:00Z chosen as start time to distinguish from CME to the W. The jet-like CME is only visible for four frames in running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2. There is no definitive source candidate on the Earth-facing disk.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement based on four faint frames of running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2. Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to lack of definitive source candidate.

note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-06-08T22:12Z. CME is also visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2. The beginning of this CME is obscured by the earlier, faster CME: 2025-06-08T21:36Z. There is no good source candidate on the Earth-facing disk, so the source is possibly far-sided. It is also possible that the source is related to some continued outflow following CME: 2025-06-08T21:36Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to lack of STEREO A COR2 imagery and lack of visible source.

note: CME first seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2025-06-08T22:24Z. CME also seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2. The start time is somewhat ambiguous as the CME does not become clearly defined until it reaches the edge of the FOV of SOHO LASCO C2. CME is much more easily distinguished in running difference imagery. There is not a good source candidate on the Earth-facing disk, so the source of this CME could be far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement based only on running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C3. While the CME is visible in SOHO LASCO C2, it is not well-defined.

note: CME first seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2025-06-09T00:36Z. CME is also seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 but not in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME could be related to some extremely faint field line movement from beyond the E limb best seen in SDO AIA 193 beginning around 2025-06-08T23:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to lack of available triangulation and lack of visible source candidate.

note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. This event is not seen in GOES CCOR-1 as it is obscured by the pylon.
